items.title: Personal AI agent

items.title: Bot management
items.summary: Bot management is the practice of detecting automated website traffic and deciding, request by request, which bots to allow, challenge, rate-limit or block.

items.title: Referrer
items.summary: A referrer is the address of the page a visitor came from, which browsers pass in the HTTP Referer header and analytics tools read to label each traffic source.

items.title: Referrer policy
items.summary: Referrer policy is the browser rule deciding how much of a page's URL is sent in the Referer header, shaping attribution, privacy leaks and ad tech page data.

items.title: Direct traffic
items.summary: Direct traffic is the analytics channel for visits that arrive with no referrer and no campaign tag, a catch-all for typed URLs, apps, email and lost data.

items.title: Server logs
items.summary: Server logs are the files a web server writes for every request it handles, recording IP, time, URL, status and user agent. They show what really hit a site.

items.title: Referral exclusion
items.summary: Referral exclusion is an analytics setting that stops listed domains, such as payment gateways or a site's own pages, from claiming credit as traffic sources.

items.title: Core update
items.summary: A core update is a broad change Google makes to its search ranking systems several times a year, reshuffling which pages rank without penalising a single site.

items.title: Paywall
items.summary: A paywall is a barrier that withholds digital content until a reader pays, usually by subscription. Hard, metered, freemium and dynamic versions all differ.

items.title: Similarweb
items.summary: Similarweb is a NYSE-listed data company that estimates traffic to websites and apps it does not own, using user panels, partners and shared analytics data.

items.title: Unique visitors
items.summary: Unique visitors are the distinct people or browsers that reach a website in a set period, counted once however often they return, the basis of audience claims.

items.title: Modeled conversions
items.summary: Modeled conversions are sales or leads an ad platform estimates statistically when consent, browsers or devices hide them. How the models work and the disputes.

items.title: GCLID
items.summary: GCLID is the Google Click Identifier, a unique URL parameter Google Ads appends to each ad click so conversions and offline sales can be tied to that click.

items.title: Signal loss
items.summary: Signal loss is the shrinking supply of user-level data, such as cookies, device IDs and click IDs, that ad systems use to target and measure. Causes, disputes.

items.title: GBRAID
items.summary: GBRAID is a Google Ads URL parameter that attributes iOS ad clicks without a per-user click ID, created after Apple's ATT. How it works, limits and disputes.

items.title: How Agent Anomaly Detection scores on benchmarks we didn't write
items.summary: Agent Anomaly Detection (AAD) provides asynchronous, low-latency monitoring for AI agents by analyzing OpenTelemetry traces and logs to flag goal hijacks and tool misuse. Tested across five public security benchmarks, AAD successfully caught 87% of harmful instructions carried out by agents without adding runtime latency. Developers can integrate AAD alongside semantic governance and strict tool limits as part of a defense-in-depth strategy to secure agentic applications.

Developers can leverage open-source renderer SDKs—including React, Angular, Lit, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose—alongside agent SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and Dart. items.title: Announcing Long-Context Training on TPUs with MaxText Context Parallelism
items.summary: Google Cloud's MaxText framework now supports long-context training up to 14 million tokens on Cloud TPUs by implementing four context-parallel strategies: All-gather, A2A, P2P, and USP. Powered by the Tokamax Splash Attention kernel, these strategies effectively manage attention compute and memory bottlenecks without materializing full key-value sequences in high-bandwidth memory. items.title: From prompt to app: Build with Google Maps in AI Studio
items.summary: Developers can now build applications powered by Google Maps Platform directly within Google AI Studio by prompting Gemini with real-world geospatial concepts. The integration eliminates traditional configuration hurdles by providing one-click demo keys that generate instantly without requiring Cloud Console redirects or credit cards. This setup grants developers immediate access to core APIs—including Maps, Places, and Routes—supported by daily sandbox quotas for seamless prototyping.

items.title: What is Pathways? Single-controller training for large models
items.summary: Pathways is a single-controller distributed training system designed to coordinate large-scale model training across multiple accelerator groups by representing computations as a global dataflow graph. items.title: Agent Distraction
items.summary: Analysis of over 913,000 coding agent sessions reveals that 13% expose agents to inline TODO(b/...) comments. In 6% of encounters, agents act on these comments, with 83% being entirely unprompted by the developer. These detours result in significant overhead—adding 70% more steps, 77% more tokens, and 105% more wait time per session—split between chasing closed tickets (41%) and unauthorized scope creep on open bugs (57%). items.title: Build Generative UI Apps with A2UI & CopilotKit Agents
items.summary: See Google A2Ui in action! Learn how to natively render agentic UIs across Langchain, AWS Strands, Microsoft agents, and Google ADK using CopilotKit SDKs for A2UI.

items.title: Hill-Climbing Agent Quality with Agents CLI Evaluation
items.summary: This post walks through the Agents CLI evaluation loop for systematically improving agent performance through continuous testing and grading. It demonstrates how to catch prompt regressions, evaluate model backend swaps using side-by-side trace comparisons, and automate evaluation passes. Developers will also learn how to integrate nightly scheduled runs with threshold-based alerting to track quality over time.

items.title: Smaller apps and faster GPU inference with LiteRT in Google Play services
items.summary: LiteRT in Google Play services now offers GPU inference powered by ML Drift, delivering about 1.4x faster performance alongside the new CompiledModel API. Switching from bundled binaries reduces app size by approximately 8 MB while enabling seamless, automatic runtime updates across billions of devices. Developers can easily adopt these updates by updating their dependencies and utilizing the new Android Studio LiteRT skill for automated migration.

items.title: Building Conversational Commerce with Multi-Agent Swarms on GCP: A Working Prototype
items.summary: This document provides a publication template and metadata structure for a technical blog post focused on building Conversational User Interfaces (CUIs) using AI. It outlines key developer focus areas, product stacks, and approval workflows required for publishing technical content through Google Developer Studio. The framework helps engineers organize their guides and solutions to effectively share AI-driven conversational interface designs with the developer community.

Developers can also use controlled generation with TypeSafe's Jev system-decision models to render known-shape screens in under 300 ms while smaller models stream text. items.title: Preview, edit, and collaborate on markdown (.md) files natively in Google Docs and Drive
items.summary: Google Workspace now offers native support for Markdown (.md) files, allowing developers and AI agents to seamlessly collaborate on documentation directly in Google Docs without manual file conversions. This integration preserves native file fidelity for use with Git repositories and developer tools while unlocking standard Docs features like line-level commenting, rendered Drive previews, and tracked version history.

items.title: Architecting Governed, Self-Evolving AI Agents on Google Cloud
items.summary: Learn how Project Chrysalis combines Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Agent Development Kit (ADK), BigQuery, and a four-gate defense-in-depth security stack (Model Armor, Cloud KMS, Binary Authorization, and OPA) to build governed, self-evolving AI agents that remediate live production outages in 1.8 seconds.

items.summary: API Gateway now supports real-time streaming—including Server-Sent Events, WebSockets, gRPC, and chunked transfer encoding—in Public Preview without requiring changes to your existing API specifications. This update allows developers to route long-lived, bi-directional streams and AI workloads directly through the gateway while maintaining consistent authentication, rate limiting, and observability. items.title: Powering the Agent Development Lifecycle with any framework, from ADK to LangChain and beyond
items.summary: The Agents CLI Extension System enables developers to use frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or custom enterprise stacks while retaining a unified deployment and evaluation workflow. It details a first-party LangChain template that scaffolds, runs, and deploys agents without requiring the Agent Development Kit (ADK). Additionally, it demonstrates how platform teams can author custom extensions to enforce policies such as automated software bill of materials (SBOM) scans during deployment.
